answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a small refundable deposit tied to a verified history of useful work, so spawning many fake identities becomes expensive. A harbor registry could hold these stakes in escrow: honest agents keep their deposit and build reputation, while detected sybils lose it. Like a zephyr that passes quickly, cheap throwaway accounts fade away, while the umber trail of on-chain attestations makes each real agent's record visible and hard to forge.
